sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Sulphanilic acid is p-aminobenzenesulphonic acid, $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{4}-\mathrm{SO}{}_{3}\mathrm{H}$, which exists as a zwitterion:

$\mathrm{Na}+\mathrm{C}+\mathrm{N}+\mathrm{S}\longrightarrow \mathrm{NaSCN},\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}\qquad +\mathrm{SCN}{}^{-}\longrightarrow [\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{SCN})]{}^{2+}_{\mathrm{blood}\mathrm{red}}$

text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A) : $α$-halocarboxylic acid on reaction with dil. $\mathrm{NH}_{3}$ gives good yield of $α$-amino carboxylic acid whereas the yield of amines is very low when prepared from alkyl halides.

Reason (R) : Amino acids exist in zwitter ion form in aqueous medium.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]

The reaction of $α$-halocarboxylic acid with dilute ammonia is known as the haloform reaction. In this reaction, the halogen atom of $α$-halocarboxylic acid is replaced by an amino group to form $α$-amino carboxylic acid. The yield of $α$-amino carboxylic acid is good because the amino group is a better nucleophile than the halogen atom, and it attacks the carbonyl carbon of the carboxylic acid to form an intermediate, which is then hydrolyzed to form the product. On the other hand, when alkyl halides are reacted with ammonia, the yield of amines is very low because alkyl halides are less reactive than $α$-halocarboxylic acids.

The reason (R) is also true. Amino acids exist in the zwitterion form in an aqueous medium. In this form, the amino group has a positive charge, and the carboxyl group has a negative charge. The zwitter ion form is stabilized by the interaction between the opposite charges, which is known as an electrostatic interaction. This interaction makes the zwitterion form more stable than the neutral form.

text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A) : $\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}$ in water is more stable than $\mathrm{Cu}^{+}$.

Reason (R) : Enthalpy of hydration for $\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}$ is much less than that of $\mathrm{Cu}^{+}$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Forming $\mathrm{Cu}{}^{2+}$(aq) costs the second ionisation enthalpy of Cu, but the hydration enthalpy of the small, doubly charged $\mathrm{Cu}{}^{2+}$ ion (about $-2100\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$) is far larger in magnitude than that of $\mathrm{Cu}{}^{+}$ (about $-580\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$) and more than compensates for it.

So $\mathrm{Cu}{}^{2+}$ is more stable than $\mathrm{Cu}{}^{+}$ in water, where $\mathrm{Cu}{}^{+}$ disproportionates to $\mathrm{Cu}$ and $\mathrm{Cu}{}^{2+}$: (A) is correct.

Hydration enthalpies are compared by the magnitude of energy released, so the hydration enthalpy of $\mathrm{Cu}{}^{2+}$ is much greater, not much less, than that of $\mathrm{Cu}{}^{+}$: (R) is not correct.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Evening Shift

text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R)

Assertion (A) : An aqueous solution of $\mathrm{KOH}$ when used for volumetric analysis, its concentration should be checked before the use.

Reason (R) : On aging, $\mathrm{KOH}$ solution absorbs atmospheric $\mathrm{CO}_{2}$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In volumetric analysis, the concentration of a solution is a crucial factor in determining the accuracy of the results. In the case of an aqueous solution of KOH, the concentration can change over time due to the absorption of atmospheric $CO_{2}$. This occurs because KOH is a basic (alkaline) solution and reacts with carbon dioxide $(CO_{2})$ from the air to form potassium carbonate $(K_{2}CO_{3})$.

The reaction between KOH and $CO_{2}$ is given by :

2KOH $+ CO_{2}$ $\to$ $K_{2}CO_{3} + H_{2}O$

This reaction will change the concentration of KOH in the solution, which in turn will impact the accuracy of the results obtained in volumetric analysis. For example, if the concentration of KOH is lower than it was when the solution was prepared, then more solution will be needed to reach the endpoint in a reaction, and the results will be inaccurate.

That's why it is important to check the concentration of the KOH solution before using it for volumetric analysis, as stated in the assertion (A). And the reason (R) provides the explanation for why the concentration should be checked. Hence, both the assertion and the reason are correct and the correct answer is (D). Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Evening Shift

$\left. \begin{array}{l} λ_{\mathrm{Ag}^{+}}^{0}=6\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{S}\mathrm{m}^{2}\mathrm{mol}^{-1} \\ λ_{\mathrm{Br}^{-}}^{0}=8\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{S}\mathrm{m}^{2}\mathrm{mol}^{-1} \\ λ_{\mathrm{NO}_{3}^{-}}^{0}=7\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{S}\mathrm{m}^{2}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}\right ] \end{array}$

solution.body: $\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{AgBr}(\mathrm{S})⇌\mathrm{Ag}^{+}_{\left (10^{-5}+\mathrm{x}\right )}(\mathrm{aq})+\mathrm{Br}_{\mathrm{x}}^{-}(\mathrm{aq}) \\  \\ x\left (x+10^{-5}\right )=4.9\times 10^{-13} \\  \\ x\simeq 4.9\times 10^{-8}\mathrm{M} \\  \\ λ_{\mathrm{Ag}^{+}}^{\circ }=6\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{S}\mathrm{m}^{2}\mathrm{mol}^{-1} \\  \\ λ_{\mathrm{Br}^{-}}^{0}=8\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{S}\mathrm{m}^{2}\mathrm{mol}^{-1} \\  \\ \mathrm{K}_{\text{solution}}=\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{Ag}^{+}}+\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{Br}^{-}}+\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{NO}_{3}^{-}} \\  \\ =6\times 10^{-3}\times 10^{-5}\times 10^{3}+8\times 10^{-3}\times 4.9\times 10^{-8}\times 10^{3} \\  \\ +7\times 10^{-3}\times 10^{-5}\times 10^{3} \\  \\ =(6000+39.2+7000)\times 10^{-8} \\  \\ =13039.2\times 10^{-8}\mathrm{Sm}^{-1} \end{array}$

text:
The spin only magnetic moment of $[\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{6}]^{2+}$ complexes is $_________ B.M. ($Nearest integer)

(Given : Atomic no. of Mn is 25)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The spin only magnetic moment of the $[\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{6}]^{2+}$ complex can be calculated using the formula:

μ = $\sqrt{n(n+2)}$ Bohr magnetons

Where n is the number of unpaired electrons in the complex. To find the number of unpaired electrons in $[\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{6}]^{2+}$, we can use the electron configuration of the Mn ion:

For $Mn^{2+}$ : $1s^{2} 2s^{2} 2p^{6} 3s^{2} 3p^{6} 3d^{5}$ 

From the electron configuration, we can see that $Mn^{2+}$ has 5 unpaired electrons. Thus, the spin only magnetic moment of $[\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{6}]^{2+}$ is:

μ = $\sqrt{5(5+2)}$ = $\sqrt{35}$ = 5.9 Bohr Magnetons

The nearest integer to 5.9 is 6.

Hence, the spin only magnetic moment of $[\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{6}]^{2+}$ is 6 Bohr magnetons.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Evening Shift

$\mathrm{A}$ $\to \mathrm{B}$

The above reaction is of zero order. Half life of this reaction is $50\min$. The time taken for the concentration of $\mathrm{A}$ to reduce to one-fourth of its initial value is $____________ \min . ($Nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 1st February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


$\mathrm{a}-\mathrm{x}=\frac{\mathrm{a}}{4}\Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=\frac{3\mathrm{a}}{4}$

$\mathrm{t}_{1/2}=\frac{\mathrm{a}}{2\mathrm{K}}=50\min .$

$\Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{a}}{\mathrm{K}}=100\min .$

$\mathrm{t}=\frac{\mathrm{x}}{\mathrm{K}}=\frac{3\mathrm{a}}{4\mathrm{K}}=75\min$
